scene.description: Barrels lying on their side are spun quickly about the vertical axis. Sliding friction at the ground contact lifts a long barrel (axial inertia smaller than transverse inertia) onto the rim of one end, where it keeps spinning and precesses. Each spinning barrel starts with a small wobble (0.5 rad/s about x and y) because a perfectly symmetric line contact gives no torque to start the rise. Left to right: long barrel at 15 rad/s, which friction stops before it can rise; long barrels at 25 and 40 rad/s, which rise about 31 degrees onto the rim and precess; long barrel at 25 rad/s with no wobble, which stays on its side while friction stops it; squat barrel at 25 rad/s, which tips onto its rim like a spun coin; long barrel with no spin as a control.
